item.title: Nature Connection Walk — Sat Nov 7, 1:30 PM — Ma Moosh Ka Win Valley Trail
item.description:
Explore Ma Moosh Ka Win Valley Trail to Highland Creek Trail (Morningside Park)! Join OLTA, CultureLink, and nature poet Sheniz Janmohamed for a guided exploration of the accessible Ma Moosh Ka Win Valley Trail at Morningside Park. Reconnect with nature and discover the beauty of the outdoors through poetry, sensory prompts, journaling, and grounding practices. This welcoming experience offers an opportunity to slow down, engage your senses, and deepen your connection with the natural world. Everyone is welcome! This event is open to people of all ages, including children and families. Activities are designed to be inclusive and accessible to people who are learning English. What to Bring
Dress appropriately for the weather Bring a water bottle or thermos

item.title: Toronto Railway Museum: From Harbour to Home: An Intro to Toronto’s Rail Lands — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — online
item.description: Toronto’s Rail Lands once covered a massive swath of the city’s downtown with railway sidings, roundhouses, and maintenance spaces. Before that, the whole area was underwater, a harbour slowly filled in by the needs of the growing railway industry. Join the TRM’s Curator of Exhibits Dumaresq de Pencier as he explores the complex and layered history of the Railway Lands, from a bustling hive of activity during the golden age of rail to the modern commuter hub that more than 45,000 people call home. Dumaresq de Pencier is an award-winning museum researcher, television presenter, exhibit developer, and guide. He has had a lifelong interest in the history of vehicular technology. He is currently curator of both the Toronto Railway Museum and the Canadian Automotive Museum in Oshawa. In his spare time he enjoys rock climbing and writing tabletop roleplaying games.
